beats.say: A thousand balls. Four thousand and ninety six possible paths. And they all build the same shape.

head: EVERY PEG:
LEFT OR RIGHT.
beats.say: At every peg, a ball bounces left or right. A coin flip. Twelve rows, so twelve flips.

head: 12 FLIPS =
4096 PATHS.
beats.say: Two choices, twelve times over. That is four thousand and ninety six different ways down.

head: MOST PATHS
END IN THE MIDDLE.
beats.say: But nine hundred and twenty four of those paths end in the middle bin. Only one path reaches each edge.

head: HIT AN EDGE?
1 IN 4096.
beats.say: So an edge is a one in four thousand and ninety six shot. Out of a thousand balls, one landed on each edge.

head: MIDDLE BIN:
243 BALLS.
beats.say: The middle bin caught two hundred and forty three. The math predicts about two hundred and twenty six.

head: THE BELL
CURVE.
beats.say: Now draw the math on top. A bell curve. Nobody aimed a single ball. Francis Galton built this board to show exactly this.
Follow Ship With Pip for more.

title: 1000 balls, 4096 paths, and they all draw the same curve
caption: A Galton board: 1000 balls, 12 rows of pegs, and at every peg a ball bounces left or right with a 50/50 chance. That is 2^12 = 4096 possible paths, and 924 of them end in the middle bin, but only 1 reaches each edge. In this run the middle bin caught 243 balls (the math predicts about 226), and 1 ball landed on each edge. Stack them up and you get a bell curve: the binomial distribution, which approximates the normal distribution. Francis Galton invented the board to demonstrate this. Every bounce here is simulated with a seeded coin flip.
notes: Seed 777, 12 rows, 1000 balls. Bin counts: [1, 3, 20, 54, 114, 187, 243, 187, 125, 48, 10, 7, 1]. 2^12 = 4096 paths; C(12,6) = 924 middle paths; expected middle = 1000 * 924 / 4096 = 225.6, about 226 (stats expected_middle_pct 22.6). Edge odds 1/4096 each. Wikipedia: invented by Francis Galton to demonstrate the central limit theorem; beads bounce left or right at pegs; binomial distribution approximates the normal. Sync: all balls released by sim 30 s, last lands at 31.6 s = start of beat 5.
